surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Devils take down the Ducks
paras: Arseny Gritsyuk struck first for the Devils early in the first, his fourth straight game with a goal. Nico Hischier made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. Tim Washe cut New Jersey’s lead to 2-1 midway through the third, but they got no closer. Anthony Mantha stretched the lead to 3-1 with less than seven minutes left, and Jack Hughes added an empty-net goal with just seven seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Devils carried the play, outshooting the Ducks 29-17, and got the result to match. Nico Daws needed only 16 saves for the Devils, and Ville Husso stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. The Devils moved to 6-4-0 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Ducks dropped to 4-6-0, fifth in the Pacific.

items.text: Jack Hughes passed Pat Verbeek for ninth on the Devils’ all-time goals list, with 171.
The Ducks are on a five-game losing streak.
The Devils got the result their play has been pointing to. Their chances have been worth about .771, better than their record (.556).
Jeff Malott and Pavel Mintyukov were in NHL.com’s projected lineup but didn’t dress.
